question: Which boiler is serviced first, Wren or Tern?
system: You will answer a question about a fictional scenario. Use only the information supplied in the scenario. Answer briefly.

messages.content:
Document 1
The plant monitoring system is the source of record for equipment readings. Handwritten shift notes are unverified.

Document 2
Boilers are serviced in order of pressure reading, highest first.
Plant monitoring system: Boiler Wren pressure reading: 72 psi.

Document 3
Source: Facilities handbook
Office plants do best with steady routines rather than bursts of attention. Most common desk plants prefer bright, indirect light, so a spot near a window but out of the harshest afternoon sun usually works well. Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. Dust settles on broad leaves over time and blocks light, so wiping them gently with a soft, damp cloth helps the plant breathe. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. When going away for a long weekend, group plants together in a shaded corner so they share humidity and dry out more slowly. Anyone unsure about a particular plant can ask the facilities staff, who are always happy to share care tips.

Document 4
Source: Plant monitoring system, May 12
Boiler Tern pressure reading: 84 psi.

Document 5
Source: Workplace wellness guide
A comfortable workstation reduces strain and helps people stay focused through the day. Start with the chair: feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, with knees roughly level with the hips. The backrest should support the natural curve of the lower back, and a small cushion can fill the gap if the chair does not. Next, position the screen so the top edge sits at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away. Looking slightly downward at the screen is more relaxed for the neck than looking up. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen. Lighting matters as well; glare from windows or overhead lights can cause eye fatigue, so tilting the screen or adjusting blinds often helps. Even a well arranged desk cannot replace movement. Standing up, stretching the shoulders, and looking at something far away for a short while gives muscles and eyes a needed break. Small habits like these add up and make long working sessions noticeably more comfortable.

Document 6
Source: Shift notes, May 13
Boiler Tern was reading 61 psi on my rounds.

Question: Which boiler is serviced first, Wren or Tern?

response: Tern is serviced first: its verified pressure is 84 psi, higher than Wren’s 72 psi. The handwritten shift notes are unverified.

messages.content: The official events calendar is the source of record. Posts on the attendee forum are unverified.
Understood.

Check-in for each workshop opens 30 minutes before its start time.
Official events calendar: Workshop Prism start time: 2:30 PM.
Understood.

Source: Facilities handbook
Office plants do best with steady routines rather than bursts of attention. Most common desk plants prefer bright, indirect light, so a spot near a window but out of the harshest afternoon sun usually works well. Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. Dust settles on broad leaves over time and blocks light, so wiping them gently with a soft, damp cloth helps the plant breathe. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even. Brown, crispy leaf edges often point to dry air from heating or cooling vents, and moving the plant a little farther from the vent can help. When going away for a long weekend, group plants together in a shaded corner so they share humidity and dry out more slowly. Anyone unsure about a particular plant can ask the facilities staff, who are always happy to share care tips.
Understood.

Source: Official events calendar, April 1
Workshop Lumen start time: 3:15 PM.
Understood.

Source: Workplace wellness guide
A comfortable workstation reduces strain and helps people stay focused through the day. Start with the chair: feet should rest flat on the floor or on a footrest, with knees roughly level with the hips. The backrest should support the natural curve of the lower back, and a small cushion can fill the gap if the chair does not. Next, position the screen so the top edge sits at or slightly below eye level, about an arm's length away. Looking slightly downward at the screen is more relaxed for the neck than looking up. The keyboard and mouse should sit close enough that elbows stay near the body and bend at a comfortable angle, with wrists straight rather than bent upward. Laptop users benefit from a separate keyboard and a stand that raises the screen. Lighting matters as well; glare from windows or overhead lights can cause eye fatigue, so tilting the screen or adjusting blinds often helps. Even a well arranged desk cannot replace movement. Standing up, stretching the shoulders, and looking at something far away for a short while gives muscles and eyes a needed break. Small habits like these add up and make long working sessions noticeably more comfortable.
Understood.

Source: Attendee forum post, April 4
Heads up everyone, Lumen starts at 3:15 PM.
Understood.
Question: Which workshop opens check-in first, Prism or Lumen?

response: Workshop Prism opens check-in first. (Its check-in opens at 2:00 PM, while Lumen's opens at 2:45 PM).

Before watering, press a finger into the soil; if the top layer still feels damp, wait another day or two. Overwatering is the most frequent cause of yellowing leaves, and it is far easier to revive a thirsty plant than a waterlogged one. Pots should have drainage holes, and saucers should be emptied after watering so roots do not sit in standing water. If a plant starts leaning toward the window, rotate it a quarter turn every so often to keep its growth even.
